filesToTouch.what: Complete the pp-007 skeleton to the full live-animals policy, WITH the two co-residency deviations that are now non-negotiable. (A) The journey prefix is a FUNCTION, never a module-load const: `const journeyPrefix = () => `${setBase()}/notifications/`` with setBase() from shared/paths.js (pp-057), which under this set resolves to '/plant-products/notifications/'. The live-animals `const JOURNEY_PREFIX = `${BASE}/notifications/`` shape is the bug class this whole increment family exists to close — a module-load capture reads the wrong set (or no set) under co-residency. pp-057 converts the live-animals file for the same reason; do not reintroduce the const form here. (A2) THE BEHAVIOURAL HALF, and it is the trap §4.6 A row 6 documents for live-animals — it applies identically here because under R7 EVERY set is mounted: `request.path` INCLUDES the mount prefix, so the guard's `startsWith(journeyPrefix())` test and its `slice(journeyPrefix().length)` journey-id extraction must both operate on the PREFIXED prefix. There is no accidental agreement to fall back on (no set sits at ''), so getting it wrong does not silently disable the guard the way it would have for a root-mounted set — it fails immediately. Pin it anyway: feed a request whose path carries '/plant-products' and assert the extracted journey id is the bare id with no leading segment and no characters eaten. (B) The policy read uses pp-005's accessor form — `systemPopulated().has(key)` called INSIDE the guard body, never hoisted to module scope. Exports: guardedJourneyPath(path) — true only for paths under journeyPrefix() that are not createPath(), not an action slug (ACTION_SLUGS = new Set(['amend','cancel-amend','copy','delete'])) and not the entry surface (importTypePage.slug or any subpath); hasCommittedNotificationAnswers(answers) — an answer counts only when its key is a manifest obligation (obligationByName), is not the flow-only 'importType' key, is not in systemPopulated() (plant policy.systemPopulated is [], so no exclusions in practice, but the code path stays uniform), and isAnswered(value); entryGuardTarget(request, h) — null for unguarded paths, null when hasEnteredThroughFilter(request, journeyId), null when hasCommittedNotificationAnswers(answers), else pagePath(request.params.journeyId, importTypePage.slug) (pagePath is a prefix-BEARING link builder, so it emits /plant-products/… automatically — never hand-prefix). Imports: shared/paths.js (setBase, createPath, pagePath), lib/answered.js, engine/read.js get, bridge/obligation-source.js accessors, flow/run-state.js, the set's features/import-type/page.js. G-E contract satisfied: entryGuardTarget returns a redirect path or falsy; its only L2 reads are engine read + run-state + obligation-source.

notes:
AMENDED FOR RULING R7 (Sam, 2026-08-01, later session) — SYMMETRIC MOUNTS. Two consequences for this increment, both about the entry guard and both cited to SIBLING-SET-PLAN §4.6 A rows 4-7. (1) The plant guard builds its journey prefix from setBase() PER REQUEST ('/plant-products/notifications/'), never from a module-load const — unchanged in substance, but the contrast case in its unit pin changes: the other context now yields '/live-animals/notifications/', not '/notifications/', because no set sits at the root. (2) NEW AND BEHAVIOURAL: `request.path` under a Hapi mount prefix INCLUDES the prefix, so the guard's startsWith test and its slice-based journey-id extraction must both use the prefixed value. This is the same trap pp-057 fixes for live-animals; here it is a build-it-right-first-time requirement rather than a migration, and it gets its own pin. Session cookies are symmetric too: plantProducts* at path /plant-products, liveAnimals* at path /live-animals — so 'a plant draft is invisible to live-animals and vice versa' is enforced by the cookie path itself on both sides, and the co-residency cases assert it in both directions.

AMENDED 2026-08-01 for Sam's ruling R3 (co-residency). This increment now sits DOWNSTREAM OF THE SESSION-SEAM REWORK, and three things change in consequence. (1) COOKIE NAMES ARE ACCESSORS, NOT CONSTANTS. By the time this runs, pp-056 has converted engine/persistence/session.js's three EXPORTED MUTABLE bindings (KNOWN_JOURNEYS_COOKIE / OPENING_RUN_COOKIE / FLOW_ONLY_ANSWERS_COOKIE) into knownJourneysCookie() / openingRunCookie() / flowOnlyAnswersCookie() resolving the current set's cookieNames. Nothing in this increment imports the old bindings, and anything that reads a cookie name reads it through the accessor. (2) THE PLANT COOKIES ARE PATH-SCOPED. routes-plant-products.js calls registerJourneyCookie(server, { base: '/plant-products', cookieNames: SESSION_COOKIE_NAMES }), so the three plant cookies carry path '/plant-products' while live-animals' carry '/live-animals' (R7 — pp-057 moved them off '/', which invalidated existing sessions; the two sets are symmetric here, neither is at the root). That makes 'a journey started in one set is invisible to the other' a testable claim, and it is now an acceptance criterion and an E2E scenario rather than an assumption. (3) THE ENTRY GUARD IS REALM-SCOPED AND MUST BE SHOWN NOT TO FIRE ON LIVE-ANIMALS ROUTES. Hapi scopes request-lifecycle extensions to the registering plugin's routes; the live-animals entry guard is already a realm-scoped onPreHandler, which is the precedent. This increment adds the behavioural pin in both directions. FOURTH AND MOST IMPORTANT: THE SET'S ENTRY GUARD MUST USE THE FUNCTION FORM OF THE JOURNEY PREFIX. `const JOURNEY_PREFIX = `${BASE}/notifications/`` — the live-animals shape — is a module-load capture and is exactly the bug class the URL work (pp-057) exists to remove; under co-residency it would bind the wrong set's base or none at all. The plant guard therefore builds its prefix from setBase() on every call, and a unit pin proves the same function yields different prefixes under different set contexts. dependsOn stays [pp-007, pp-008]; pp-056/pp-057 (P-9/P-10) are covered transitively through pp-007→pp-006. Division of labour vs pp-017 unchanged: this increment owns MECHANICS (guard, opening run, session commit, resume); pp-017 owns the full page spec. Guard unit tests still need a non-empty manifest to prove hasCommittedNotificationAnswers=true — compose a fixture set via configureObligationSet(setId, …) (bridge characterisation-test pattern), noting the seam now takes a setId first. Rulings applied: R3, FD-3 (plantProducts* cookie names, now load-bearing), FD-8, FD-13, FD-14/FD-15/FD-16/FD-17, §4.2 rows 6/8/10/11, c-018/c-004/c-014 recorded once in docs/README.md. Exemplars (transpose, do not invent): sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/flow/entry-guard.js (policy shape — but NOT its JOURNEY_PREFIX const), flow/run.js, features/import-type-filter/controller.js, and shared/paths.js + shared/set-context.js as pp-056/pp-057 landed them.
